title: Completion of coherent modules is an exact functor
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] whose underlying space is quasi-compact) and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals. The category $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)$ of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent] and the category $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] are abelian [def-sp-abelian] ([lem-weil-pbc-abelian-full-subcategory-exact], [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian]), and the completion functor $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (2), $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F^\wedge=(\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)_{n\ge1}$, $u\mapsto u^\wedge=(u\bmod\mathcal I^n)_n$, is exact: it is additive and carries every short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ of $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)$ to a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'^\wedge\to\mathcal F^\wedge\to\mathcal F''^\wedge\to0$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence] (for an additive functor between abelian categories this is Stacks' 'exact', i.e. commuting with finite limits and finite colimits, by Homology, Lemma 010N (4)).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0881 (lemma-exact, line 6423), functor (0880) (equation-completion-functor); affine reduction via Lemma 087X (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian) (3) and Lemma 087W (lemma-inverse-systems-affine) to Algebra, Lemma 00MB (lemma-completion-flat) (2)

proof.text: (The two abelian categories and additivity.) $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)$ is the full subcategory of the abelian category $\mathit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] of the coherent modules. It contains $0$, and kernels, cokernels and finite direct sums in $\mathit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ of maps between coherent modules are coherent ($X$ is locally Noetherian) [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth] (1); every object of $\mathit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ isomorphic to a coherent module is coherent [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-modules-kernel-cokernel-sum] (3). By [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-full-subcategory-exact], $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)$ is abelian and a sequence $0\to\mathcal F'\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{v}\mathcal F''\to0$ of coherent modules is short exact in $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)$ iff it is short exact in $\mathit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is abelian with termwise addition of morphisms [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian]. The completion functor is a functor [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (2), and it is additive: for $u,u':\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$, $(u+u')\bmod\mathcal I^n$ and $(u\bmod\mathcal I^n)+(u'\bmod\mathcal I^n)$ both composed with the epimorphism $\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ give $q^{\mathcal G}_n\circ(u+u')$, hence agree, and morphisms of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ are added termwise. So it remains to show that it carries short exact sequences to short exact sequences; fix $0\to\mathcal F'\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{v}\mathcal F''\to0$ short exact in $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)$. Its completion $0\to\mathcal F'^\wedge\to\mathcal F^\wedge\to\mathcal F''^\wedge\to0$ is a complex ($v^\wedge u^\wedge=(vu)^\wedge=0$).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01Y0 (lemma-coherent-abelian-Noetherian) and Modules, Lemma 01BY (5) for Coh(O_X); Lemma 087X (1) for Coh(X, I); the functor (0880) before Lemma 0881

proof.text: (Reduction to an affine covering: 'it suffices to check this locally on $X$'.) Since $X$ is locally Noetherian with quasi-compact underlying space, there are finitely many affine opens $U_1,\dots,U_r$ covering $X$ with $A_j=\mathcal O_X(U_j)$ Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. For an open $V\subseteq X$ and a coherent $\mathcal F$, $(\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)|_V=(\mathcal I|_V)^n(\mathcal F|_V)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (3) (by induction on $n$, applying (3) also to $\mathcal I\cdot\mathcal I^n$), and cokernels of $\mathcal O_X$-modules commute with restriction to $V$ (sheafification of the sectionwise quotient commutes with restriction) [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; hence $\rho_V(\mathcal F^\wedge)=(\mathcal F|_V)^\wedge$ with the same transition maps and $\rho_V(u^\wedge)=(u|_V)^\wedge$, where $\rho_V$ is the restriction functor of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-local-exactness] (1). By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-local-exactness] (2), applied to the covering $\{U_j\}$, the completed sequence is short exact in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ as soon as, for every $j$, $0\to(\mathcal F'|_{U_j})^\wedge\to(\mathcal F|_{U_j})^\wedge\to(\mathcal F''|_{U_j})^\wedge\to0$ is short exact in $\mathit{Coh}(U_j,\mathcal I|_{U_j})$. Fix $j$ and write $U=U_j$, $A=A_j$, $I=\mathcal I(U)$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0881, first sentence ('It suffices to check this locally on X. Hence we may assume X is affine'), by Lemma 087X (3)

proof.text: (Sections over $U$.) By step 1 the sequence is short exact in $\mathit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, so $u$ is a kernel of $v$ [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-short-exact-kernel] and $v$ is a cokernel of $u$ [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-exact-epi-cokernel] (a). Kernels in $\mathit{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$ are sectionwise [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so (comparing the kernel $u$ with the sectionwise kernel of $v$ by the isomorphism of kernels) $u_U:\mathcal F'(U)\to\mathcal F(U)$ is injective with image $\ker v_U$. Coherent modules are quasi-coherent [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], so by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (3) the cokernel $q:\mathcal F\to\operatorname{Coker}u$ has $q_U$ surjective with kernel $u_U(\mathcal F'(U))$; $v$ differs from $q$ by an isomorphism $\operatorname{Coker}u\cong\mathcal F''$, so $v_U$ is surjective with kernel $u_U(\mathcal F'(U))$. Hence with $M'=\mathcal F'(U)$, $M=\mathcal F(U)$, $M''=\mathcal F''(U)$ the sequence $0\to M'\xrightarrow{u_U}M\xrightarrow{v_U}M''\to0$ of $A$-modules is exact, and $M',M,M''$ are finitely generated $A$-modules, since coherent modules are quasi-coherent of finite type [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] and such a module has finitely generated sections over an affine open [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0881 (a coherent module on X = Spec(A) is a finite A-module, Lemma 01XZ); the exactness of sections over an affine open is implicit there

proof.text: (The affine description.) Identify $U$ with $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; since $\mathcal I|_U$ is quasi-coherent, the counit $\widetilde I\to\mathcal I|_U$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (3), so $\mathit{Coh}(U,\mathcal I|_U)$ is the category of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] for $(A,I)$, and $E:(\mathcal G_n)\mapsto\varprojlim_n\Gamma(U,\mathcal G_n)$ is an equivalence of $\mathit{Coh}(U,\mathcal I|_U)$ with the category $\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}_{A^\wedge}$ of finitely generated $A^\wedge$-modules, $A^\wedge$ the $I$-adic completion, with quasi-inverse $G:N\mapsto((N/I^nN)^\sim)_n$ [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] (2). By [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (2), $\Gamma(U,\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)=M/I^nM$ with the canonical surjections as transition maps and $\Gamma(U,u\bmod\mathcal I^n)=u_U\bmod I^n$. Hence $E((\mathcal F|_U)^\wedge)=\varprojlim_nM/I^nM=M^\wedge$ and $E((u|_U)^\wedge)=(u_U)^\wedge$, the completions of [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] (likewise for $\mathcal F',\mathcal F''$, $v$): $E$ carries the restricted completed sequence to $0\to M'^\wedge\to M^\wedge\to M''^\wedge\to0$. This is the identification of the functor with 'the functor $\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}_A\to\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}_{A^\wedge}$ which associates to a finite $A$-module $M$ the completion $M^\wedge$'.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0881, second and third sentences, via Lemma 087W (lemma-inverse-systems-affine)

proof.text: (Exactness of completion on finite modules.) $A$ is Noetherian and $M',M,M''$ are finitely generated (step 3), so $0\to M'^\wedge\to M^\wedge\to M''^\wedge\to0$ is an exact sequence of $A$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules]; the maps are $A^\wedge$-linear, so it is an exact sequence of $A^\wedge$-modules. $A^\wedge$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], hence $\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}_{A^\wedge}$ is abelian and this sequence is a short exact sequence of $\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}_{A^\wedge}$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-modules-noetherian-abelian].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Lemma 0881, last sentence ('Thus the result follows from Algebra, Lemma 00MB'), Algebra Lemma 00MB (2)

proof.text: (Back along the equivalence.) $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a Noetherian scheme, so $\mathit{Coh}(U,\mathcal I|_U)$ is abelian [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian]. The quasi-inverse $G$ of step 4 is additive: on morphisms $G(f)=((f\bmod I^n)^\sim)_n$, and $f\mapsto f\bmod I^n$ and $f\mapsto\widetilde f$ are additive ($\widetilde f$ is determined by $\widetilde f_U\circ\tau=\tau\circ f$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (1)); and it is an equivalence between abelian categories. So $G$ carries the short exact sequence of step 5 to a short exact sequence of $\mathit{Coh}(U,\mathcal I|_U)$ [lem-weil-pbc-equivalence-injective-resolutions] (2). The natural isomorphism $\mathrm{id}\cong G\circ E$ of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] (2) gives, by naturality, an isomorphism of complexes from $0\to(\mathcal F'|_U)^\wedge\to(\mathcal F|_U)^\wedge\to(\mathcal F''|_U)^\wedge\to0$ to $G$ of $0\to M'^\wedge\to M^\wedge\to M''^\wedge\to0$ (step 4); a complex isomorphic to a short exact sequence is short exact (monomorphisms, epimorphisms, images and kernels are carried along isomorphisms) [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. Hence the restricted completed sequence is short exact in $\mathit{Coh}(U_j,\mathcal I|_{U_j})$ for every $j$, and by step 2 the completed sequence is short exact in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$. With step 1, the completion functor is exact.
